files.title: Your files
files.description:
Apple's SF Pro font and the SF Symbols glyphs cannot ship with this integration, so they live in a folder of your own under /config, served at /hk/ ahead of the bundled files. It survives integration updates.

Put the font at fonts/SF-Pro.woff2 (or fonts/SF-Pro.ttf, as Apple ships it) and the glyph data at iconset/hk-glyphs.js.

Found now: font {font}, glyphs {glyphs}.

data_description.files_folder: For example hk_local. Everything in it is readable without signing in, like /local/, so use a folder that holds nothing else.

missing_font.title: SF Pro font not added
missing_font.description: HK Frontend is designed around Apple’s SF Pro, which can’t ship with it. Download SF Pro from {fonts_url} and copy SF-Pro.ttf (the variable font) to /config/{folder}/fonts/ — or, smaller, a SF-Pro.woff2 made from it with tools/font/make_woff2.py from {repo_url}. Until then the screens use Roboto. How: {guide_url}

missing_glyphs.title: SF Symbols glyphs not added
missing_glyphs.description: The hk: icons are Apple’s SF Symbols, which can’t ship with HK Frontend. On a Mac with the SF Symbols app, build /config/{folder}/iconset/hk-glyphs.js with tools/sf_symbols/build_glyphs.py from {repo_url}. Until then each hk: icon is drawn as the Material Design icon of the same name, and the weather with Material’s weather icons. How: {guide_url}

ha_too_old.title: Home Assistant is too old for HK Frontend
ha_too_old.description: This is Home Assistant {version}. The HK pages are built and tested against {minimum} or newer, and older frontends draw them wrongly. Update Home Assistant (Settings → System → Updates).

theme_missing.title: HK Kiosk theme not loaded
theme_missing.description:
The HK pages draw their colors, font and glass from the HK Kiosk theme. HK Frontend loads it itself, and this time it could not (the log says why). You can load it from configuration.yaml instead:

1. In configuration.yaml, under `frontend:`, add `themes: !include_dir_merge_named themes` (skip this if you already load themes from a folder).
2. Create `/config/themes/hk_kiosk.yaml` containing the single line `!include ../custom_components/hk_frontend/theme/hk_kiosk_theme.yaml`
3. Developer tools → YAML → **Themes** (or restart).

This message clears itself once the theme loads.

energy.title: Energy
energy.description: An Energy page for your screens: the whole home’s power and today’s cost, a fortnight of daily use, and a live tile for each circuit, room, appliance and outlet. It starts from Home Assistant’s own Energy settings (Settings → Dashboards → Energy); its sections, names and rows are then on the HK Settings page, Features → Energy. A screen shows it once Energy is on its Pages, or pick “Energy Display” when you add a screen.

alarm_pin.title: Add a PIN to an alarm
alarm_pin.description:
For an alarm that arms and disarms for anyone who asks (it takes no code of its own). Alarm PIN adds a second alarm panel that mirrors it and arms or disarms it only with this PIN. A wrong PIN is refused, so any keypad shows "Wrong code". Point your keypads and dashboards at the new panel; automations can keep using the alarm itself.

The PIN is never stored or shown: only a secure hash of it is kept.

data_description.alarm: Its own settings should take no code.
data_description.pin_again: Type it once more, so a slip can’t be saved.
data_description.arm_required: Off: arming needs no PIN (one that is given must still be right). Disarming always needs it.

alarm_pin_options.title: Alarm PIN
alarm_pin_options.description: The PIN is never shown: type a new one twice to change it, or leave both empty to keep the current one.

data_description.alarm: Choose another to move the PIN and its panel to it; the PIN and the arm rule stay the same. Its own settings should take no code.
data_description.pin: At least 4 characters. Both empty keeps the current PIN.
data_description.pin_again: Type it once more, so a slip can’t be saved.
data_description.arm_required: Off: arming needs no PIN (one that is given must still be right). Disarming always needs it.

clean_areas.title: Clean Areas
clean_areas.description: Clean chosen areas with whichever vacuums can reach them, from each vacuum's room map in Home Assistant. Pick which vacuums take part.

data_description.vacuums: Empty: every vacuum. Each one's rooms come from its room map in Home Assistant (the vacuum's own entity settings). One that cannot clean by area starts when its own area is chosen; one with clean-by-area but no room map is skipped (for example a second integration's copy of the same robot).

Empty: every vacuum. Each one's rooms come from its room map in Home Assistant (the vacuum's own entity settings). One that cannot clean by area starts when its own area is chosen; one with clean-by-area but no room map is skipped (for example a second integration's copy of the same robot).
data_description.areas: Which areas the vacuum area picker offers. Empty: every area a vacuum that takes part can reach (by its room map, or its own area for one that only starts).
